chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abd al-Rahman al-Arzmee from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you catch the Imam on Friday [for prayer] and he has already led you in one rak'ah, add another rak'ah to it and recite aloud in it. If you catch him while he is reciting the Tashahhud, then pray four [rak'ahs]."

key_terms.أَرْبَعًا: Four (referring to the number of rak'ahs)
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: The leader of the congregational prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَةٍ: A unit of prayer (bowing and prostration)
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ: On Friday (referring to the Friday prayer)

ai.seo_question: How many rak'ahs should one pray if they join the Friday prayer late?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the variable structure of the Friday prayer for latecomers, distinguishing between catching the Imam in the first rak'ah versus the sitting position. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the validity of joining the congregational prayer at different stages, ensuring the worshipper fulfills their obligation correctly whether they join during the recitation or the final testimony. This specific guidance highlights the practical application of *ijtima'* (congregation) in Shia fiqh, ensuring the latecomer's prayer is complete and valid according to the Imam's actions.
